title: Meridian field evaluation
description: The complete schema for TWO record types of the practical-evaluation contract: record_type field-evaluation-observation (one measured data point about ONE metric of ONE execution run, scoped to run-state and pinned to that run) and record_type field-evaluation-report (a deterministic aggregation over a pinned, externally-resolved set of observations, scoped to project-workspace, never a single rolled-up score). A record declares THIS schema in its $schema, so a consumer that follows the declaration validates the whole record — the reused scoped-record envelope AND the specialised body — in one pass. The envelope is the SAME contract as registries/operating-model/scoped-record.schema.json; scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs validates every record against scoped-record.schema.json directly as well. Which body shape applies is selected by record_type (allOf/if/then below), not by a second schema file. The eight characteristics of meridian-operating-upgrade-plan.md §10 are modelled separately (never one score): mechanism-correctness, context-entry-time, rework-returns, stop-correctness, missed-norms, resumption-success, owner-cost, post-acceptance-defects. Each has a closed measurement kind — classification / duration / count — fixed per metric_id; a classification's outcome pool is closed per metric and its basis is never the bare run status. An observation's status is one of observed / unknown / not_applicable / unmeasurable — four distinct states, each but 'observed' carrying a reason, because absence of observation is not zero. Every calendar date and timestamp of this contract (observed_at, observation_period, the report's period, measurement start_ts/end_ts) is checked for REAL calendar existence — the length of the specific month, leap years — not merely a digit pattern; 31 February, 31 April and a non-leap 29 February are rejected, never silently rolled over the way Date.parse would. Status 'observed' requires at least one PINNED evidence entry RESOLVED through the external boundary to a closed evidence-result confirming observed_result 'confirmed' AND a metric_ref naming THIS observation's own metric — evidence of a different metric is rejected. A correction is a NEW observation that pins the one it supersedes with a correction_reason; the superseded record is never edited in place. A report pins a set of included and excluded observations (each reasoned) that are kept DISJOINT — no reference, and no resolved observation id, is shared between the two lists, and no excluded reference repeats under a different reason — checks them for the SAME workspace and the SAME reporting period, rejects double counting (a repeated id, or a superseded+superseding pair both included), represents every one of the eight metrics exactly once, and RECOMPUTES — for EVERY status, known/unknown/not_applicable alike — each metric's aggregate from the resolved, named sample: a report that diverges from what its own observations show is rejected regardless of the status it claims. Every observation referenced by a report is resolved through the SAME THREE-PART boundary everywhere in this module, never a lighter, ad hoc check and never a second divergent copy of the pinned_ref rule: (1) checkPinnedRef on the INPUT pinned_ref ITSELF — its own record_type is strictly field-evaluation-observation, it carries a stable semantic id, a portable reference, and a pin (an exact revision and/or sha256) — checked independently of whatever the resolver later returns, because resolvePinnedReference alone only cross-checks a pin field's value WHEN that field happens to be present on the input ref and does not itself require id, record_type or a pin to be present at all; (2) resolvePinnedReference on the RESOLVED record — its record_type, the closed key set with no extra field, id and reference matching the pin, and an exact revision and/or confirmed digest matching what was pinned; (3) resolvedObservationIssues on the resolved record's subject VALUES (metric_id, status, measurement, workspace_id, observed_at, supersedes_id, observation_period, coverage all checked for validity, not merely for the closed key set) — only once (1) and (2) are clean. A problem at ANY of the three is a precise, named error, never a silent omission: an invalid or unresolvable record, a wrong record_type (on the input ref OR on the resolved record), a missing id, a missing pin, an unexpected field, or a mismatched digest/revision all make the deterministic report builder (buildFieldEvaluationReport) fail closed with an explicit thrown error rather than building a report around it. A correction (supersedes) and the observation it corrects are never both included: the builder rejects that pair immediately with a thrown error, rather than silently dropping one from the aggregate, auto-preferring the correction, or returning a report for evaluateFieldEvaluation to reject afterwards. A ratio always carries both a numerator and a denominator; a zero denominator forbids a percentage. The rules this JSON Schema subset cannot state live in scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs (the declared $schema resolves as a LOGICAL address within the Meridian namespace — resolveSchemaRef/nonPortableReason reused from scripts/lib/task-specification.mjs via scripts/lib/context-manifest.mjs; the metric-to-measurement-kind and classification-outcome-pool mappings; strict calendar-date/time validity; the external resolution AND validated projection of every pinned reference and evidence entry; the comparability, disjointness and double-counting rules; the exact recomputation of every per-metric aggregate at every status; the fail-closed, canonically-ordered — by resolved id with the reference as an unambiguous tie-break — deterministic report builder; portability of every reference and prose string; the Russian name). The contract is a MANDATORY part of the Kernel: an absent schema or absent fixtures is a validator FAIL, not an informational skip. The normative document is standards/workspace/meridian-field-evaluation.md.

pinned_ref.description: A closed, structured, pinned reference to exactly one record — execution-run or field-evaluation-observation in this contract. No record body is embedded: the object is closed to these fields only. revision and/or sha256 pin the exact edition (checked in scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs).

scope_ref.description: An evaluation record's area: run-state for an observation (scope.id equals execution_run_ref.id and workspace_id is mandatory), project-workspace for a report (scope.id is the report's own id; workspace_id lives in the payload instead, because project-workspace scope does not carry one).

origin.description: Same contract as scoped-record.schema.json's origin. Evaluation data is written in a workspace, so kind 'built-in' is additionally rejected by scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs.

classification_measurement.description: A classification of ONE instance (one stop event, one norm-application opportunity, one resumption attempt, one mechanism check) for a metric whose measurement kind is 'classification'. outcome must be one of that metric's own closed pool (checked in scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs, which also fixes WHICH metrics use this kind). basis is the stated reason for the classification — never the bare run status or work_status by itself, and an 'unknown' outcome is never silently counted as the tracked positive/negative outcome.

duration_measurement.description: A duration for a metric whose measurement kind is 'duration'. duration_kind distinguishes calendar length from active effort — the two are never summed into one figure. unit is always 'seconds'. seconds is non-negative. paused_seconds (only valid with duration_kind 'calendar') is the time subtracted to reach an active-effort figure, and cannot exceed seconds. start_ts/end_ts, when both present, name an interval whose end is strictly after its start (checked in scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs).

count_measurement.description: A non-negative integer count for a metric whose measurement kind is 'count'.

evidence_entry.description: One piece of evidence grounding ONE observation's measurement. id is a stable semantic identifier, unique within the record. kind is one of a closed set. reference is a portable, storage-neutral pointer, PINNED by an exact revision and/or a SHA-256 digest (checked in scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs). summary states what was observed. Every evidence entry is RESOLVED through the external boundary to a closed 'evidence-result' carrying observed_result (confirmed / contradicted / inconclusive) AND metric_ref — the metric this evidence bears on; an observation's status 'observed' needs at least one entry that resolves with observed_result 'confirmed' and metric_ref equal to this observation's own metric_id.

observation_payload.description: The bounded body of one field-evaluation observation, as a CLOSED object. It carries a structured pinned reference to the run (never the run's body); the metric it measures; when it was itself recorded; one of four statuses (observed / unknown / not_applicable / unmeasurable), each non-'observed' status carrying status_reason and no measurement, 'observed' carrying a measurement matching the metric's own fixed kind and no status_reason; a required, non-empty evidence list only when 'observed'; observation_period + coverage only for metrics that declare a window (post-acceptance-defects), only while 'observed'; and an optional supersedes + correction_reason pair naming, with a reason, the earlier observation this one corrects.

excluded_observation_entry.description: One observation deliberately left out of the report's computation, with the reason stated — an exclusion is explicit, never a silent drop. If the excluded observation would have contributed to a metric, that metric's per_metric entry must disclose it as a limitation (checked in scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs).

classification_aggregate.description: The recomputed aggregate for a classification metric: counts per closed outcome, their total, and a rate whose numerator/denominator are both always present. A zero denominator (no classified sample) forbids the percentage field.

duration_aggregate.description: The recomputed aggregate for a duration metric: calendar length and active effort are two SEPARATE sub-aggregates, never summed into one total (a sample contributes to exactly one of the two, by its own duration_kind).

count_aggregate.description: The recomputed aggregate for a count metric. observation_window and coverage appear only for a metric that declares a window (post-acceptance-defects); coverage 'mixed' means contributing observations disagreed on completeness.

per_metric_entry.description: ONE of the eight characteristics, represented separately — never folded into another. metric_id is one of the closed eight, and the full per_metric array carries each EXACTLY once (checked in scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs). status 'known' carries no status_reason and an aggregate recomputed from the named sample; 'unknown' / 'not_applicable' carry a status_reason and an aggregate reflecting an empty or inapplicable sample. sample_observation_ids names which included observations contributed, all belonging to this metric_id. limitations discloses gaps the aggregate alone does not show — including a disclosed exclusion and the explicit caveat that a zero post-acceptance-defect count over a partial window is not proof of no defects.

report_payload.description: The bounded body of one field-evaluation report, as a CLOSED object. workspace_id names the project workspace it covers (project-workspace scope carries no workspace_id itself, unlike run-state). period is the reporting window. included_observations and excluded_observations are separate, pinned, externally-resolved lists — an exclusion always carries a reason. per_metric carries exactly the eight closed characteristics, each with an aggregate recomputed from its own resolved sample, never a single rolled-up score (forbidden fields are rejected by scripts/lib/field-evaluation.mjs).
